MC	<p>ab84_967c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1d5dac;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cej, +++, cej"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #87388f;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #87388f;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #87388f;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ekw, +++, ekw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6f43a9;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, amt, +++, amt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>1393_06f6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #934225;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #934225;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #934225;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4b6903;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1d5dac;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hjx, +++, hjx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>cc99_0313</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4b6903;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #96336a;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #96336a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #96336a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cep, +++, cep"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0938_24b8</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #87388f;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #87388f;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #87388f;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jrw, +++, jrw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>2393_b30c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1d5dac;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #96336a;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #96336a;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #96336a;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bdf, +++, bdf"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7955_f50a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a0303f;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4a4dc0;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cpx, +++, cpx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ae30_2ac9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #686001;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #686001;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #686001;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #96336a;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #96336a;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #934225;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #934225;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #934225;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4a4dc0;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, adh, +++, adh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>082a_0df2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #a0303f;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #686001;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #686001;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #686001;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4a4dc0;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bcf, +++, bcf"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>43c2_4f01</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #96336a;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #96336a;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #96336a;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ktw, +++, ktw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>749e_d999</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6f43a9;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hpy, +++, hpy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>bbb9_0f02</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6f43a9;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jpt, +++, jpt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7338_54d1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6f43a9;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hkm, +++, hkm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5aa9_abc8</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #686001;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #686001;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #686001;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #87388f;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #87388f;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #87388f;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, abj, +++, abj"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a9c0_2de0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #686001;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #686001;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #686001;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6f43a9;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fmx, +++, fmx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #187032;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #187032;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #187032;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #87388f;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #87388f;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #87388f;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, drx, +++, drx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f02f_bfff</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #934225;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #934225;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #934225;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1d5dac;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ejx, +++, ejx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>82c8_3a3b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a0303f;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4a4dc0;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, adw, +++, adw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4a4dc0;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>854c_4b99</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #934225;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #934225;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #934225;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4a4dc0;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dnp, +++, dnp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>dc4c_59dd</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1d5dac;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, emn, +++, emn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #a0303f;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4b6903;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4a4dc0;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hpy, +++, hpy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7b9e_cfef</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #a0303f;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4b6903;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1d5dac;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>1be0_bcfd</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #87388f;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #87388f;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #87388f;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, djt, +++, djt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #686001;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #686001;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #686001;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6f43a9;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ctw, +++, ctw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #686001;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #686001;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #686001;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #87388f;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #87388f;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #87388f;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #87388f;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>783a_f56b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #a0303f;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4b6903;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4a4dc0;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, erw, +++, erw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>12b3_4de6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #934225;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #934225;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #934225;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4b6903;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4a4dc0;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, abh, +++, abh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #a0303f;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #4a4dc0;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hkw, +++, hkw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>890a_06f7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #87388f;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #87388f;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>64bb_54e1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a0303f;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #4b6903;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1d5dac;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fmx, +++, fmx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5782_37d7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #934225;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #934225;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #934225;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4b6903;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1d5dac;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mwy, +++, mwy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #686001;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #686001;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #686001;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #96336a;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #96336a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #96336a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bhp, +++, bhp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4a4dc0;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hpx, +++, hpx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>145b_fa67</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #4a4dc0;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cdy, +++, cdy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f001_e072</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8b4c00;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b4c00;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6f43a9;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, afw, +++, afw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006691;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006691;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006691;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #96336a;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #96336a;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #96336a;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, npx, +++, npx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>850a_0190</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #934225;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #934225;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #934225;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #4b6903;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4b6903;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6f43a9;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, prt, +++, prt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>e0f4_ae92</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1d5dac;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #96336a;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #96336a;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #96336a;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ctx, +++, ctx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>60cf_9d74</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6f43a9;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hjt, +++, hjt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5944_8e03</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #a0303f;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #686001;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #686001;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #686001;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a0303f;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4a4dc0;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cmt, +++, cmt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9418_3398</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #686001;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #686001;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #686001;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #87388f;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #87388f;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #87388f;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ckr, +++, ckr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
