MC	<p>0a4e_0086</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #686001;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #686001;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #686001;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00697c;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #00697c;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00697c;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6f43a9;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f43a9;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, aty, +++, aty"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006c6a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006c6a;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #87388f;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #87388f;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 MC	<p>0fa2_d423</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7a5700;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a5700;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1d5dac;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1d5dac;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #96336a;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #96336a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>40fb_cee4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a0303f;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a0303f;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006e55;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006e55;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006e55;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4a4dc0;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4a4dc0;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cdx, +++, cdx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
